subject: Weekly Exec Thermometer: OKR heatmap & QBR asks
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Weekly Exec Thermometer: OKR heatmap & QBR asks

Good morning — quick, compact read for leadership distro ahead of the QBR dry run next week. PDF and a checklist attached. TL;DR and asks at the top.

Wins:
- Serving runtime: rolling deploy of the new KV-cache allocator completed on stage; 12% median p95 token latency improvement for internal benchmarks.
- Dedication pilot: two mid-market customers (AcroSoft, Nimbus pilot) signed up for Dedicated trial — ramp plan in play.
- Console observability: token-level cost dashboard landed; early feedback is actionable (engineering has a follow-up).

Risks / Heatspots:
- Model onboarding backlog: 3 community models flagged for quantization regressions; research estimates 10 work-days to stabilize (blocks some demo variants).
- Capacity/ops: Dedicated burst scheduling surfaced intermittent throttle under sustained 40k rps — mitigation in progress but could affect QBR demo throughput.
- QBR narrative: we have two competing metrics (latency vs unit-cost) in the draft deck; need leadership guidance on prioritization for executive narrative.

Asks (what I need from you this week):
1) Laura — confirm which metric we prioritize in the QBR executive slide: business-facing unit-cost reduction OR p95 latency improvements? (I recommend unit-cost for CFO audience; latency for product ops audience.)
2) Karthik — can Platform commit an owner to the Dedicated burst gate remediation by Tue EOD (owner + 48h plan)?
3) Vanessa — can you pair runtime numbers with customer impact vignettes (one-liners) for AcroSoft and Nimbus by Wed?
4) Soojin — ops: please prepare a 1-slide mitigation swimlane for the capacity issue for the QBR dry run.

Notes: attached heatmap shows team-level OKR progress (green/yellow/red) and the CSV includes the QBR checklist with owners pre-filled where possible. I’ll loop in Nina (Nimbus) after we lock the customer-facing bullets.

Thanks — short replies appreciated so I can pull the deck together.

—
Jasmine Liu
Director, Product Strategy, Redwood Inference
(jasmine.liu@redwood.com)

Attachments: 2026_Q2_OKR_heatmap.pdf, QBR_prep_checklist.csv

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly Exec Thermometer: OKR heatmap & QBR asks

Thanks, Jasmine — useful and crisp. My quick guidance: prioritize unit-cost on the single executive headline (CFO + GTM hearing) and keep latency as the operational callout on slide 2.

Also: add a short mitigation table (top 3 risks) with owners and 'impact if unresolved' (revenue/ops/customer). Example: Dedicated burst gate (owner: Platform infra) — impact: demo throughput and committed trials.

On the model onboarding backlog, please mark the affected demos so we can decide whether to swap in verified variants for the QBR.

On Tue we can decide whether to invite Nina for a 15-min walk-through; tentatively agree after we have Vanessa's customer vignettes.

On Tue 2026-06-23 I have 10–10:30 AM available for a run — if that works for the team.

—
Laura
VP, Operations
